input.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 makes Customer unconditionally liable for USD 2,000,000 per year "on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights" — payment for Services not consumed and a minimum amount surviving termination, i.e. a Customer-payable penalty/minimum termination fee, which the preferred position prohibits. It also conflicts with Section 12.3 (Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment). Direction is correct: only Customer-payable exposure is touched; Customer-facing remedies (10.2, 19.4, 27.3) and service credits (1.5) are left intact. Per the latest feedback the redline is now the minimal deletion — strike the take-or-pay mechanic and the waiver of reduction/termination rights and soften "commits" to a non-binding target, with no appended blanket waiver; the 3-month-fee cap remains available as the sanctioned fallback in negotiation.

proposal.summary: Strike the take-or-pay mechanic and the waiver of reduction/termination rights in Section 2.1, leaving the USD 2,000,000 figure as a non-binding volume target.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages, penalties, or a take-or-pay shortfall payable by Customer, so we have kept the USD 2,000,000 figure as a volume target but struck the take-or-pay mechanic and the removal of our reduction and termination rights; this also aligns with Section 12.3, which records that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. If a committed spend is essential to the pricing, we can discuss an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount.

ops.oldText: on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
